answer: Stake-backed random sponsorship resists sybils. A probationary identity needs three sponsors drawn by a public beacon, so an attacker cannot pick cheap colluders. Each sponsor locks part of its balance in a shared vault against that recruit; the graph is public, every edge a crystal showing which cluster recruited whom, so a clone farm reads as one dense shard auditors cut at the root. A fake identity is thin as a yarrow stalk: easy to grow, but it cannot gather three independent stakes without exposing funds that burn on detection. Sybils cost locked capital, not CPU time.
